recent_deploys.message: fix: collector otelcol.signal scope attribute conflict in logs pipeline (#3321)

ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy 2b8ccac18a70 (2026-05-13T12:00:40Z) bumped the swoosh dependency and incidentally updated analyticsservice/config/scheduler.exs, which rescheduled the nightly order_items aggregation job to run at 11:42 UTC (mid-day production peak) instead of the previously configured 02:00 UTC maintenance window. The aggregation job issues a long-running full-table scan with a ShareLock on public.order_items (pid=3817), blocking autovacuum from reclaiming dead tuples. As dead tuple bloat accumulated (dead_tuples exceeded 3.1M), sequential scan performance degraded ~40%, causing query latency to spike. Combined with the lock queue depth growing to 63+ waiting queries, the PostgreSQL connection pool (max=100) became fully exhausted, triggering HTTP 503 responses across productcatalogservice and checkoutservice.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately terminate the blocking analytics query: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(3817); — this will unblock autovacuum and drain the lock wait queue within seconds. 2. Revert analyticsservice/config/scheduler.exs from deploy 2b8ccac18a70 to restore the 02:00 UTC schedule, or hot-patch the scheduler config to move the job outside peak hours. 3. Once autovacuum runs and the connection pool drains, verify dead tuple counts return to normal with: SELECT relname, n_dead_tup FROM pg_stat_user_tables WHERE relname='order_items'; 4. Add a statement_timeout of 300s for the analytics role to prevent future unbounded queries from blocking autovacuum indefinitely: ALTER ROLE analytics_user SET statement_timeout = '300s';
